name: Boji Stones
toxicityNote: Contains iron sulfide that can oxidise; keep dry and wash hands after handling.

Crystal healers link it to circulation of energy

summary: Boji Stones are iron concretions from the American plains, worked in male-female pairs and valued for balance, grounding and gentle energy tingles.
intro: Boji stones are natural concretions, small rounded or flattened nuggets of iron minerals formed layer by layer in sandstone over millions of years. They come in two types: smoother, rounder pieces called male, and flatter, pitted, more irregular ones called female. Colours are rusty brown to dark grey, often with a metallic sheen from pyrite or marcasite inside. Tapped together, a pair is said to feel a pulse in the palms, and many users report a warm or tingly sensation when holding them. The stones are usually sold in pairs, from tiny pocket-sized to fist-sized pieces. Their compact, earthy look makes them favourites for bodywork and meditation.
history: The name Boji, sometimes spelled Bojii, was popularised by crystal writer Robert Simmons, who described the stones in the 1980s, and Kansas collectors had long gathered similar concretions from sandstone cliffs. The main source is the Ottawa and Saline regions of Kansas, where iron-rich groundwater cemented around tiny cores of sand. The stones are sometimes called Kansas pop rocks, since the pairs are said to give off a mild vibration or popping feeling. Geologists regard them as ordinary concretions, found in many parts of the world, but the American versions became known in metaphysical circles. They have no ancient folk tradition; the use of Boji stones is a recent addition to crystal practice.
meaning: Boji stones are used for balance, particularly of polarity. In crystal tradition, the pair of male and female stones represents yin and yang, and holding one in each hand is said to harmonise left and right, giving a centred feeling. Practitioners link them with the Root and Earth Star for grounding, and the Solar Plexus for personal energy. Many people report a gentle tingling or pulse in the hands, which they interpret as energy flow. The stones are popular in energy work, where they are placed on or around the body or laid in the hands during meditation. They are considered grounding and stabilising rather than flashy, ideal for those who feel scattered. These are traditional associations and not medical claims.
howToUse: Hold one stone in each hand during meditation, rest the pair on the lap or place them on the floor beside you. Tap them gently together to feel any vibration. Lie down and rest a pair at the hips or ankles for a grounding visualisation. Keep the pair on a desk or nightstand together, as they are usually kept as a set. Pair them with quartz points in a grid for a stable foundation. Keep them dry and handle gently, as they can crumble with age.
care: Boji stones contain iron sulfide and can rust or crumble if kept damp, so avoid water entirely and store them in a dry place, perhaps with a silica gel packet. Wipe with a dry soft brush. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or by resting them on a selenite plate. Sunlight is safe. Keep the pair together in a pouch or box, apart from harder stones. Wash your hands after handling, and do not make elixirs.
identify: Genuine Boji stones are dense, rough concretions with a rusty or metallic crust, and the male type is smoother and rounder while the female is flatter with pits and projections. Fakes include polished or painted hematite, man-made iron balls and moulded pieces. Real ones are not uniform, with bumps and irregular surfaces and varied weights. They are often sold in matched pairs; the energy claims have no scientific support, so judge them on appearance, authenticity of source and personal experience.

faq.a: They are iron-rich concretions found mainly in Kansas, sold as male and female pairs. Their rounded and pitted forms are used in crystal practice for balance, grounding and gentle energy work.
